extracted.intended_audience: sociolinguists, conversation analysts, pragmatics researchers and students studying humor in everyday talk
extracted.subtask_description: Framework for identifying, classifying, and evaluating joking turns in ordinary conversation (forms, timing, structural devices, functions, and uptake). Intended to guide analysis of humor as it operates in interaction rather than isolated joke texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of analysis: joking turn
rubrics_metrics.description: The unit of analysis is the joking turn in talk, not the joke text in isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the joking turn within sequential interaction: how it is produced, responded to, and situated in the flow of conversation. Avoid analyzing joke text stripped of its conversational context, since timing, uptake, and local relevance are central to how humor functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canned jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-formed, stand-alone joke texts inserted into the conversation. Marked entry: 'Did you hear the one about...' or 'That reminds me of a joke.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristics: conversation pauses for the joke; joke completes; conversation resumes. Function: often conversational interludes rather than substantive contributions. Consider how insertion point and marked entry affect uptake and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal anecdotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Narratives of personally experienced events told for comic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Builds conversational currency (the speaker presents themselves through the story). Funnier when artfully shaped via selection of detail and pacing. Implicit truth claim ('this actually happened') influences how recipients interpret and respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneous wordplay
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit that exploits something just said in the conversation (puns, re-construals, allusion-triggers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates quick uptake and is closely tied to the immediate local context. Success depends on tight timing (arriving close to the trigger) and recipients' ability to link the play to the prior turn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony and sarcasm
rubrics_metrics.description: Saying the opposite of what is meant, often with tonal cues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires shared interpretive ground. Can be friendly or hostile depending on relationship and target; tone and context determine whether it functions as rapport-building or aggression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual teasing / banter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks closeness — only friends can banter without offense. Has its own conversational rhythm where turns get returned in kind; track the pattern of exchanges to evaluate safety and uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition as structural device
rubrics_metrics.description: Joking turns frequently use repetition: words/phrases or whole structural patterns reappear with new framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms include returning a prior word/phrase with new framing, escalating lists, rule-of-three patterns. Repetition signals 'this is a joke' by deliberately patterning ordinary speech and provides a resource for recipients to recognize the play frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-stage vs. multi-stage processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-stage: comic recognition is immediate. Multi-stage: the joke unfolds over multiple turns (stories building to a punch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversational humor mixes both types; skilled humor production times sharp, immediate gibes alongside extended setups. Analyze whether recognition occurs within the same turn or across turns and how that affects uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing differences: wordplay vs. narrative jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Word play depends on tight timing — the comic word must arrive close to the trigger; narrative jokes require pacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wordplay requires proximity to its trigger to register; narratives need controlled pacing — too slow loses the audience, too fast collapses the buildup. Evaluate timing relative to the trigger and the sequence of turns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional axis: aggression vs. rapport
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversational humor can serve aggression (putting down, asserting dominance) or rapport (building intimacy, signaling alignment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same surface joke can operate on either axis depending on relationship, tone, and uptake. Assess function by examining target, relationship between participants, tonal cues, and recipients' responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listener cues and uptake
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversational humor is not complete until the listener responds: laugh, returned witticism, echoed phrase, nod or smile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the listener fails to uptake (silence, deflection, return to seriousness), the humor is ineffective regardless of textual quality. In analysis, treat uptake as constitutive of humor and document recipient responses and any repair moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: recognized play frame
rubrics_metrics.description: Both speaker and hearer are oriented to the comic mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shared orientation to 'this is play' is required for the joke to be recognized as humorous rather than taken literally or seriously. Look for markers that establish the play frame (repetition, formulaic openings, paralinguistic cues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: local relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The joke arises out of, and refers back to, the immediate conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local relevance ties the comic move to prior turns; 'you had to be there' effects rely on this. Evaluate whether the joke leverages immediate context, references, or prior talk for its effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: appropriate pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing matches the joke's structural type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different joke forms require different pacing (see timing differences entry). Assess whether the speed and rhythm of delivery fit the form (wordplay vs. narrative) and support recipient recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary condition: functional fit (appropriateness to relationship)
rubrics_metrics.description: The humor's aggressive/rapport function is appropriate to the relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A joke's acceptability and effect depend on whether its function fits the social relationship and setting. Evaluate relational history, power dynamics, and whether recipients treat the move as affiliative or hostile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic checklist for analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Set of questions to guide analysis: form, processing stage, local relevance, uptake, function and appropriateness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these questions to diagnose individual joking turns: - What conversational form is the humor (canned joke, anecdote, wordplay, irony, banter)? - Is the comic move single-stage or multi-stage? - Is the joke locally relevant — arising from the conversation? - Does the listener uptake it? - Is the function aggression or rapport — and is that function appropriate to the relationship? These function as an operational checklist for coding and interpretation.
